{{Quote|If the surgery fails, I will have lost nothing.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="COF" />}}
Following the [[Battle of Devaron/Legends|escape of]] [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]] from the [[Resolute/Legends|''Resolute'']] over [[Devaron/Legends|Devaron]], the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] abducted several infants from their homes. The [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] planned on using these children to create an army of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Spy/Legends|spies]]. After finding traces of volcanic ash on Bane's [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], the [[Xanadu Blood/Legends|''Xanadu Blood'']], and evidence of the bounty hunter's travels to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in his fueling records, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] '''investigated''' a facility on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]].

==Prelude==
In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Sidious]] began to rely on the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]], who was considered to be the most efficient gun-for-hire in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] following the [[Death/Legends|death]] of renowned [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]]. Bane was tasked with stealing a [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]] and the [[Kyber memory crystal/Legends|Kyber memory crystal]], which contained a list of every single [[The Force/Legends|Force]] sensitive infant in the galaxy. Bane was then tasked with taking four children on the list to Sidious's lab on [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], a volcanic [[Mining/Legends|mining]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. Bane succeeded in taking [[Zinn Toa/Legends|Zinn Toa]], a [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]], and [[Wee Dunn/Legends|Wee Dunn]], a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]], but was arrested during his [[Attempted kidnapping of Roo-Roo Page/Legends|attempted kidnapping]] of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Roo-Roo Page/Legends|Roo-Roo Page]]. Following a harsh interrogation session, the bounty hunter led [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to [[Black Stall Station/Legends|his base of operations]], though this was a trap set up to ensure his own escape.<ref name="COF" />

While Windu and Kenobi were away on their mission, the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] inspected Bane's [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], the [[Xanadu Blood/Legends|''Xanadu Blood'']], which had traces of volcanic ash on its hull. While Bane had wiped his navigation records, he had failed to wipe his fueling records, which revealed the four planets Bane had been to in his recent travels: [[Glee Anselm/Legends|Glee Anselm]], [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]], Mustafar, and [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Mustafar was the only planet on the list that was volcanic, and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were previously unaware of his travels there. Skywalker and Tano traveled to Mustafar in the [[Twilight/Legends|''Twilight'']] to investigate.<ref name="COF" />

==The mission==
As soon as the ''Twilight'' landed on Mustafar, one of the [[Nanny droid/Legends|nanny droids]] watching over the missing children, [[RO-Z67/Legends|RO-Z67]], reported to Darth Sidious that a ship had landed, and it wasn't Bane. Sidious quickly ordered for the [[Gravity well/Legends|gravity supports]] to be deactivated and for the children to be evacuated to his [[Darth Sidious's secondary facility/Legends|secondary facility]]. Hearing the wails of Wee Dunn, Tano guided Skywalker to the children's chamber using the Force. RO-Z67 deactivated the gravity supports as Darth Sidious commanded, and retrieved the children from their cradles. The droids deactivated the lights as the Jedi cut their way into the room using their [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]]. While Tano thought the worst when they found two empty cradles, Skywalker still sensed their presence, and the two nanny droids emerged from the shadows, using the children as human shields. The facility was beginning to collapse, and Tano managed to secure Toa, slicing the droid's arms off, while Skywalker retrieved Dunn from RO-Z67 after the droid was forced to let go of the child to cling for its life. With the children safely rescued, the Jedi retreated to the ''Twilight'' just as the facility was completely destroyed.<ref name="COF" />

==Aftermath==
Skywalker and Tano brought the children back to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]. Since the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] wasn't sure of the extent of what the children were subjected to on Mustafar, the Council decided to not return the children to their parents and instead raise them in the Temple, at least for the time being.

Since the entire base sank into the lava, the Jedi were unaware of Darth Sidious's involvement since any evidence of his involvement was destroyed. As Cad Bane escaped from Obi-Wan Kenobi and Mace Windu at Black Stall Station, a follow up interrogation was impossible. Despite this, the children were safe, and the holocron was recovered, with no sign of its information being duplicated. However, [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] remained concerned about the future of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] following the incident.<ref name="COF" />

==Behind the scenes==
New technology introduced during production of [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|season two]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' made it possible to fit Mustafar and several other planets depicted in "[[Children of the Force]]" into the timespan of a single episode.<ref name="comment">{{SW|url=video/children-of-the-force-episode-featurette|text="Children of the Force" Episode Featurette}}</ref>

Director [[Dave Filoni]] was initially opposed to including Mustafar in the show, since that would mean Skywalker and the other characters would be aware of the planet's existence during [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. [[George Lucas]] later persuaded him, clarifying that since Mustafar was a mining planet, it had to have had exports and been an active member of the galactic community.<ref name="comment" />
